title: Ang 1380–1384: Farid's saloks, second half
hookLine: the Creator in creation, every heart a jewel
tomorrow: Guru Arjan praises the One for pages. does God even need praise?

lines: A REPLY FROM OUTSIDE THE THREAD.
cards: Sometimes the best comment on a post comes from someone who wasn't in the original thread. Farid's pages have something like that.

Here and there among his couplets sit saloks under the Gurus' own headings, answering him, turning his lines, carrying them further. It's an odd thing to find in a scripture: a conversation across the page.
And near the end comes the answer to yesterday's question. Farid says every heart is a jewel.

teach.h: THE GURUS WRITE INTO FARID'S PAGES.
teach.b: First the puzzle: why would the Gurus write into someone else's pages? Readers hear it as respect, not correction.
Where Farid is harsh with himself, a Guru's salok sometimes turns the line gently, and the two voices stand side by side. The Granth keeps the whole conversation in view.

Then the line, on ang 1384, in paraphrase: every heart is a jewel; to break any one is not good at all. If you long for the Beloved, don't break anyone's heart. A few pages earlier, Farid gives the reason.
In paraphrase: the Creator is in creation, and creation lives in God. So whom can we call bad? There is no one without Him.
Put those two together and the jewel makes sense.

teach.h: PRECIOUS FOR WHO LIVES IN IT.
teach.b: A heart is precious because of who lives in it. Breaking one isn't only unkind; it's breaking something the Beloved lives inside.
It's close to what Kabir sang at dawn, from one light, here said in a Sufi's language of longing: the Beloved, the jewel, the heart.

how: Sikhs often quote Farid's 'every heart is a jewel' on kindness; in the Granth his saloks are read together with the Gurus' saloks set among them.

games.q: Farid's couplets, second half — tap the pairs.
p: in creation, and creation in God

s: the Gurus' words never appear inside a Bhagat's section
among Farid's couplets sit saloks under the Gurus' own headings, answering him.
Farid says every heart is a jewel
and to break any one is not good at all.
Farid means 'don't break the hearts of good people'
he says any heart. whom can we call bad, when the Creator is in creation?

games.q: a friend's ex is getting roasted in the group chat, and it's honestly funny. everyone's waiting for your reaction. what does ang 1384 point to?
o: don't add to it; every heart is a jewel, an ex's included.
a reaction emoji isn't really breaking a heart, so it's fine.
call out everyone in the chat as cruel, loudly, by name.
games.why: Farid says any heart, and gives the reason: the Creator lives in creation. not joining in doesn't mean breaking the other hearts in the chat either.

practice: Pull up a photo of one person, someone you love or someone you find hard. Look at their face through the sit, and let the word jewel rest beside it. Nothing to say.

wordCard.voice: Ang 1380. The second half of Farid's couplets, where the Gurus answer him and every heart is called a jewel.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: maanik, a jewel, from Farid's salok on ang 1384: every heart is a jewel.

carryVoice: Hold onto this: every heart a jewel, even the ones that are hard to like. Back tomorrow.
